answer: We define a Sybil-resistant mechanism for oracle networks deployed across a maritime wharf, riparian willow ecosystem, and tidal inlet using dynamic opportunity-cost bonds paired with a zero-knowledge delay-slashing matrix. An adversary creating k identities incurs superlinear staking costs B(k), forcing expected attack payoff E[U] = R(k) - B(k) - L * P(slash) < 0 for all k > 1. Thus, rational multi-agent interaction converges to a unique subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium that renders identity proliferation strictly unviable.
